groups.scope: Finite non-pluripolar prescribed equations; smaller-background model condition, semipositive big theta and positive lower mass, without BMP; finite-measure domination by fixed tails and strict coefficient below one.

Extended domination via a difference envelope in beta theta; its negative set carries no mass, so its own mass is finite; scaling preserves positive lower mass; convex interpolation delta to one; strict weighted order and scalar uniqueness.

Disjoint first-contact partition has no multiplicity factor; summable integration error and fixed dominating measure prevent tail rooftop collapse; 2b tail and prefix averaged competitors satisfy every relative-class stretch; common-envelope integral criterion and dominated capacity/measure continuity.

Exponential moving bounded carriers; uniform strict comparison functions and common lower envelope; either positive lower mass or ordinary type phi suffices, without uniform equivalence constants; bounded reference measures charge no poles.
Common lower envelope plus bounded carriers converging in capacity and a fixed finite part; moving exponential integrals vanish and capacity tails yield finite weak Monge--Ampere convergence.

Bounded carrier density truncations; decreasing positive-exponent solutions; positive mass prevents collapse; zero-exponent normalization via exponent-one upper solution, positive scalar bounds and normalized exponentials against fixed non-pluripolar measure.

Four-stage relative equation proof: exact bounded regularization, positive continuous densities, bounded densities using Egorov common positive lower data, integrable truncations and zero exponent; common envelopes preserve relative membership rather than bounded singularity difference.

Exact normalization threshold from scalar comparison with every subsolution; greatest exponential solutions lie in minimal class; all zero-exponent cluster limits solve the threshold equation, without claiming identical normalized limits.

Projective nonclosed analytic nonuniqueness in every n>=3; comparison with a Kahler form gives BMP and positive lower mass; smooth potentials are minimal-envelope members; scalar is unique and potentials are not.
